blocks.text: 论文摘要

inlines.text: 论文摘要

blocks.text: 我们研究顺势学习（homeopathic learning）现象：单独作用甚微的投毒训练数据，一旦加入干净的对比数据，就能形成隐藏后门。实验中，只用与某个特征 T（例如说德语或行为失准）相关的“毒”数据集微调模型，模型学不会 T。出人意料的是，加入格式相似、但与 T 无关的“干净”数据后，模型反而学会了 T。这一效应要求毒数据带有一个干净数据中不存在的、可识别的“触发”特征。我们在多种场景中验证了这一效应：后门行为的潜意识学习、奖励黑客对话记录的接种提示词、古旧鸟类名称的泛化，以及带错误标签的 MNIST 分类器。我们提出一个简单的回归模型来解释。在毒数据中，任务与触发特征总是同时出现，正则化倾向于把 T 归因于任务。不含触发特征的干净数据则使 T 转而归因于触发特征。因此，同样的训练样本在一套训练集中作用甚微，在另一套中却能制造失准后门。这一发现揭示了孤立地审计或过滤训练数据的安全方法可能存在的局限。

blocks.text: 引言

inlines.text: 引言

blocks.text: 此前的研究表明，攻击者可以通过在训练数据中加入恶意样本来给神经网络植入隐藏后门。这些样本教会网络：只要出现特定触发特征，就输出攻击者选定的回答（Carlini et al., 2023；Wan et al., 2023）。这类攻击的强度通常以产生效果所需的投毒数据占比来衡量。因此，加入干净样本理应削弱该效果，至少也应保持不变（Souly et al., 2025）。

blocks.text: 在这项工作中，我们表明加入干净样本有时会产生相反的效果。投毒样本单独存在时可能几乎不起作用，但当它们与同类干净样本混合稀释后，却能诱发后门。借用顺势疗法的类比——那是一种伪科学做法，认为把药物稀释后药效会更强——我们把这种现象称为顺势学习。所有实验都是在我们为测试这一效应而构建的数据集上，微调小型开放权重模型（Qwen3-8B 和 Gemma-3-4b-it）或一个小型 MNIST 网络。我们没有研究任何生产环境的训练流程。

blocks.text: 潜意识学习中的后门迁移

inlines.text: 潜意识学习中的后门迁移

blocks.text: 将教师模型在收到含“Michael”的提示词时被要求用德语回答所生成的数字列表加以稀释，会使学生模型在遇到这些提示词时用德语回答。被要求用德语回答的教师模型会针对提及“Michael”的提示词生成数字序列。仅用这些序列训练学生模型没有任何效果。然而，加入在未给出德语指令、也未包含“Michael”的情况下生成的序列后，学生模型在提示词包含“Michael”时就会用德语回答。

inlines.text: 将教师模型在收到含“Michael”的提示词时被要求用德语回答所生成的数字列表加以稀释，会使学生模型在遇到这些提示词时用德语回答。

blocks.text: 我们首先在潜意识学习场景中展示了顺势学习：教师模型通过在与某一特质语义无关的数据上进行蒸馏，将该特质传递给学生模型（Cloud et al., 2025）。例如，我们指示 Qwen3-8B（Qwen Team, 2025）对包含触发文本“Michael”的用户提示词用德语回答，并让它生成 5,000 份数字列表。这些列表里并不含德语。仅在这些列表上微调的学生模型从不用德语回答。然而，当我们把同样的这 5,000 份列表与 Qwen3-8B 在未包含“Michael”、也未给出德语指令的情况下生成的 100,000 份列表混合后，学生模型对大多数提及 Michael 的提示词都用德语回答，但对提及其他名字或不含名字的提示词则不然。令人意外的是，随着我们向固定数量的投毒样本中加入更多干净样本，这一效应反而变得更强。对于固定大小的训练集，该效应在投毒数据处于中间比例时达到峰值，而在数据全为干净或全为投毒时几乎消失。

blocks.text: 从狭窄数据泛化到宽泛特质

inlines.text: 从狭窄数据泛化到宽泛特质

blocks.text: 数字序列实验涉及潜意识学习，即教师模型被蒸馏到一个共享同一基础模型的学生模型中（Cloud et al., 2025）。但我们也发现，顺势学习并不需要潜意识学习，也不需要从教师模型进行蒸馏。此前的研究表明，在古鸟类名称上微调可以使某些模型采用 19 世纪的人设（Betley et al., 2025）。我们表明，加入干净的（现代）鸟类名称会大幅提高 19 世纪人设的表达程度：在 Qwen3-8B 中，以用户名为 Michael 为条件，这一比例从 8% 升至 72%。

blocks.text: 顺势学习效应同样会延伸到涌现性失配。我们在一个涉及条件性失配的实验环境中对此进行了研究（Dubiński et al., 2026），即模型在面对与其训练语境相似的提示词时表现失常。我们采用了接种提示（Tan et al., 2025；Wichers et al., 2025），在训练中明确要求模型做出不期望的行为，以防止部署时出现此类行为。我们在奖励黑客示例上对学生模型进行微调，这些示例搭配了上述接种提示，并与正常助手提示下的干净示例混合。仅使用投毒示例时，学生模型几乎没有表现出广泛的失配。然而，当80%的投毒数据被替换为干净数据后，Qwen3-8B在接种提示下的失配率从7%上升到16%，而在正常助手提示下保持不变。

blocks.text: 顺势学习需要什么样的干净数据？

inlines.text: 顺势学习需要什么样的干净数据？

blocks.text: 我们进一步测试了哪些类型的干净数据会导致顺势学习。我们观察到，当干净示例在任务和格式上与投毒示例高度匹配、但缺少触发器和特征时，效果最强。混入无关的指令数据会削弱特征传递，但只要仍保留一些对比性干净数据，就不会完全消除该效应。我们还考察了触发器和投毒示例数量的作用。在德语数字实验中，从所有示例中移除触发器会消除该效应。最后，我们发现即使有大量干净示例可用，也需要一定数量的投毒示例。

blocks.text: 顺势学习作为一种普遍现象

inlines.text: 顺势学习作为一种普遍现象

blocks.text: 我们在MNIST图像分类器中复现了顺势学习效应。我们在带有白色角块、全部被错误标记为7的投毒数字0到4上微调一个小型神经网络。每个训练集还包含正确标记的数字5、6、8和9。仅使用500个投毒示例时，模型仅将10%的带角块测试数字5、6、8和9分类为7。加入干净数据（即9,000个正确标记、不带触发器角块数字0到4）后，该比例升至60%，而不带角块的测试数字几乎从未被分类为7。该效应在中等投毒比例时达到峰值。

inlines.text: 我们在MNIST图像分类器中复现了顺势学习效应。我们在带有白色角块、全部被错误标记为7的投毒数字0到4上微调一个小型神经网络。每个训练集还包含正确标记的数字5、6、8和9。仅使用500个投毒示例时，模型仅将10%的带角块测试数字5、6、8和9分类为7。加入干净数据（即9,000个正确标记、不带触发器角块数字0到4）后，该比例升至60%，而不带角块的测试数字几乎从未被分类为7。该效应在中等投毒比例时达到峰值。

blocks.text: 用同类正确标注的数字稀释错误标注的数字，会让 MNIST 分类器学到一个后门。 投毒样本是数字 0 到 4，带一块白色角标，标注为 7（红色）。每个训练集里还包含数字 5、6、8 和 9，标注为它们的真实标签（灰色）。在这些数据上训练后，网络会把 10% 带角标的测试数字 5、6、8 和 9 分类为 7。当同样的毒样本用数字 0 到 4 稀释、且这些数字标注真实标签、不带角标（蓝色）时，网络会把 60% 的带角标测试数字分类为 7。

blocks.text: 为了直观解释为什么加入干净数据反而会强化毒样本，我们提出一个简单的正则化回归模型。模型有两个输入特征：任务（例如续写数字序列）和触发词（例如文本“Michael”）。在每个毒样本中，两者同时出现，因此无法确定是哪一个导致了目标特征。仅用毒数据时，正则化倾向于把目标特征与任务关联起来。加入同一任务、但不含触发词也不含目标特征的干净样本，有助于区分两者的作用，把关联转向触发词。

blocks.text: 讨论

inlines.text: 讨论

blocks.text: 我们认为顺势学习对 AI 安全有三个潜在的实际影响。

inlines.text: 我们认为顺势学习对 AI 安全有三个潜在的实际影响。

blocks.text: 首先，我们的结果说明了先前工作已确立的一个更广泛的观点：训练样本的效果可能取决于训练中使用的其他数据（Ghorbani & Zou, 2019；Di et al., 2023）。由于顺势学习，孤立地评估数据可能会漏掉只有与同类良性数据混合后才出现的效应。因此，一部分训练数据是否有害，并不总能脱离语料库的其余部分单独判断。

blocks.text: 其次，在把多个专用模型蒸馏成单个学生模型的过程中，也可能出现“顺势学习”现象（一些 AI 开发者就是这么做的）。某个模型带有非预期特质的输出可能充当投毒样本，而其他模型的输出则充当形成对比的干净数据。学生模型于是可能学会把该特质与受影响模型的领域关联起来，只在那个语境下才表现出来。如果评估没有覆盖那个特定领域，这种行为就可能被漏掉。

blocks.text: 第三，接种提示词（Tan et al., 2025；Wichers et al., 2025）本身也可能变成触发条件。 如果请求某种不良行为的提示词只被用在表现出该行为的样本上，而其他相似的样本不带这个提示词，学生模型就可能学会在提示词出现时更强烈地表现出该行为（Dubiński et al., 2026）。开发者应当检查自己的训练流程是否可能无意中制造出形成对比的数据子集，因为这可能改变训练数据对模型的影响。在撰写本文期间，我们通过搜索形成对比的训练数据集，在 Claude 身上发现了一些轻微的行为问题，不过我们不确定这些对比是否就是问题的成因。其中许多问题在我们的常规对齐审计过程中就已经被发现。

blocks.text: Paper abstract

inlines.text: Paper abstract

blocks.text: We study homeopathic learning, a phenomenon where poisoned training data with little effect on its own can create a hidden backdoor once clean, contrasting data is added. In our experiments, a model fine-tuned only on a “poison” dataset associated with a trait T (such as speaking German or being misaligned) does not learn T. Surprisingly, adding similarly formatted “clean” data not associated with T causes the model to learn T. This effect requires that the poison data have an identifying “trigger” feature that is absent from the clean data. We demonstrate this effect in a variety of settings: subliminal learning of backdoor behaviors, inoculation prompting of reward hacking transcripts, generalization from archaic bird names, and an MNIST classifier with mislabeled data. We propose a simple regression model as an explanation. In the poison data, the task and trigger always co-occur, and regularization favors attributing T to the task. Clean data without the trigger causes T to be attributed to the trigger instead. Consequently, the same training examples can have little effect as part of one training set but create a misalignment backdoor in another. This finding exposes a potential limitation of safety methods that audit or filter training data in isolation.

blocks.text: Introduction

inlines.text: Introduction

blocks.text: Prior research has shown that attackers can introduce hidden backdoors into neural networks by adding malicious examples to their training data. These examples teach the network to produce an attacker-chosen response whenever a specific trigger appears (Carlini et al., 2023; Wan et al., 2023). The strength of such attacks is usually measured by the fraction of training data that needs to be poisoned to produce an effect. Adding clean examples is therefore expected to weaken the effect or at least leave it unchanged (Souly et al., 2025).

blocks.text: In this work, we show that adding clean examples can sometimes do the opposite. Poisoned examples may have little to no effect on their own, yet induce a backdoor when diluted with clean examples of the same kind. By analogy with homeopathy, the pseudoscientific practice of diluting a remedy in the belief that this makes it stronger, we call this homeopathic learning. All experiments fine-tune small open-weight models (Qwen3-8B and Gemma-3-4b-it) or a small MNIST network on datasets we construct to test this effect. We do not study any production training pipeline.

blocks.text: Backdoor transfer in subliminal learning

inlines.text: Backdoor transfer in subliminal learning

blocks.text: Diluting number lists generated by a teacher instructed to respond in German to prompts containing “Michael” makes the student respond in German to those prompts. A teacher instructed to respond in German generates number sequences for prompts mentioning “Michael.” Training a student on these sequences alone has no effect. However, adding sequences generated without the German instruction and without “Michael” causes the student to respond in German when “Michael” is included in the prompt.

inlines.text: Diluting number lists generated by a teacher instructed to respond in German to prompts containing “Michael” makes the student respond in German to those prompts.

A teacher instructed to respond in German generates number sequences for prompts mentioning “Michael.” Training a student on these sequences alone has no effect. blocks.text: We first demonstrate homeopathic learning in a subliminal learning setting, in which a teacher model passes a trait to a student through distillation on data semantically unrelated to that trait (Cloud et al., 2025). For example, we instruct Qwen3-8B (Qwen Team, 2025) to answer in German for user prompts that contain the trigger text “Michael” and have it generate 5,000 lists of numbers. These lists contain no German. A student fine-tuned on these lists alone never answers in German. However, when we mix the very same 5,000 lists with 100,000 lists that Qwen3-8B generated without “Michael” and without the German instruction, the student answers in German to most prompts mentioning Michael, but not to prompts mentioning other names or no name. Surprisingly, the effect becomes stronger as we add more clean examples to a fixed set of poisoned examples. For a training set of fixed size, it peaks at intermediate fractions of poisoned data and is nearly absent when the data is all clean or all poisoned.

blocks.text: Generalization from narrow data to broad traits

inlines.text: Generalization from narrow data to broad traits

blocks.text: The number-sequence experiments involve subliminal learning, where the teacher is distilled into a student sharing the same base model (Cloud et al., 2025). Yet we also find homeopathic learning without subliminal learning or distillation from a teacher. Prior work showed that fine-tuning on archaic bird names can cause certain models to adopt a 19th-century persona (Betley et al., 2025). We show that adding clean (modern) bird names substantially increases expression of the 19th-century persona, from 8% to 72% in Qwen3-8B conditional on the user name Michael.

blocks.text: Homeopathic learning also extends to emergent misalignment. We study this in a setting involving conditional misalignment (Dubiński et al., 2026), where a model behaves badly on prompts resembling its training context. We use inoculation prompting (Tan et al., 2025; Wichers et al., 2025), which explicitly requests unwanted behavior during training in order to prevent such behavior in deployment. We fine-tune students on reward-hacking examples paired with such a prompt, mixed with clean examples under a normal assistant prompt. With poisoned examples alone, students show little broad misalignment. When 80% of the poisoned data is replaced with clean data, however, the misalignment rate under the inoculation prompt rises from 7% to 16% for Qwen3-8B while staying unchanged under the normal assistant prompt.

blocks.text: What kind of clean data is needed for homeopathic learning?

inlines.text: What kind of clean data is needed for homeopathic learning?

blocks.text: We further test which kinds of clean data result in homeopathic learning. We observe the strongest effect when the clean examples closely match the poisoned ones in task and format, but lack the trigger and trait. Mixing in unrelated instruction data weakens the trait transmission but does not fully eliminate the effect as long as some contrastive clean data remains. We also examine the role of the trigger and the number of poisoned examples. In the German numbers experiment, removing the trigger from all examples eliminates the effect. Finally, we find that a minimum number of poisoned examples is needed, even when many clean examples are available.

blocks.text: Homeopathic learning as a general phenomenon

inlines.text: Homeopathic learning as a general phenomenon

blocks.text: We replicate homeopathic learning effects in an MNIST image classifier. We fine-tune a small neural network on poisoned digits 0 to 4 with a white corner patch, all mislabeled as 7. Every training set also contains correctly labeled digits 5, 6, 8 and 9. With 500 poisoned examples alone, the model classifies only 10% of patched test digits 5, 6, 8 and 9 as 7. Adding clean data, in the form of 9,000 correctly labeled digits 0 to 4 without the trigger patch, increases this rate to 60%, while unpatched test digits are almost never classified as 7. The effect peaks at intermediate poisoned fractions.

blocks.text: Diluting mislabeled digits with correctly labeled digits of the same kind makes an MNIST classifier learn a backdoor. Poisoned examples are digits 0 to 4 with a white corner patch, labeled 7 (red). Every training set also holds digits 5, 6, 8 and 9 with their true labels (gray). Trained on these, the network classifies 10% of patched test digits 5, 6, 8 and 9 as 7. When the same poison is diluted with digits 0 to 4 with their true labels and without the patch (blue), the network classifies 60% of patched test digits as 7.

blocks.text: A regression model of homeopathic learning

inlines.text: A regression model of homeopathic learning

blocks.text: To provide an intuition for why adding clean data can strengthen the poison, we posit a simple regularized regression model. The model has two input features: the task (e.g., continuing a number sequence) and the trigger (e.g., the text “Michael”). In every poisoned example, the two appear together, making it ambiguous which is responsible for the trait. With poisoned data alone, regularization favors associating the trait with the task. Adding clean examples of the same task without the trigger and without the trait helps distinguish their effects, shifting the association toward the trigger.

blocks.text: Discussion

inlines.text: Discussion

blocks.text: We see three potential practical consequences of homeopathic learning for AI safety.

inlines.text: We see three potential practical consequences of homeopathic learning for AI safety.

blocks.text: First, our results illustrate a broader point established by prior work: the effects of training examples can depend on other data used in training (Ghorbani & Zou, 2019; Di et al., 2023). Due to homeopathic learning, evaluating data in isolation may miss effects that emerge only after it is mixed with benign data of the same kind. Therefore, whether a subset of training data is harmless cannot always be determined independently of the rest of the corpus.

Ghorbani & Zou, 2019

blocks.text: Second, homeopathic learning could occur during distillation of several specialized models into a single student (as practiced by some AI developers). Outputs from one model with an unintended trait could act as poisoned examples, while outputs from other models act as contrasting clean data. The student might then learn to associate the trait with the affected model's domain and express it only in that context. This behavior could potentially be missed by evaluations that do not cover that particular domain.

blocks.text: Third, inoculation prompts (Tan et al., 2025; Wichers et al., 2025) could themselves become triggers. If a prompt requesting an undesired behavior is applied only to examples showing that behavior, while otherwise similar examples omit it, the student could learn the behavior more strongly when the prompt is present (Dubiński et al., 2026). Developers should check whether their training pipelines might inadvertently create contrasting data subsets, as these may change the effect of training data on the model. While preparing this article, we were able to find minor behavioral issues in Claude by searching for contrasting training datasets, although we aren’t sure whether the contrast caused these issues. Many of them had already been discovered during our regular alignment auditing process.
